MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    Clicking, locking, exclude meniscal tear..

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination. The extensor mechanism is intact. There is patella alta. The Insall Salvati ratio measures about 1.6.
The finding is associated with advanced patellofemoral joint osteoarthritic change with extensive denuding of the articular cartilage and with extensive subcortical cyst formation particularly seen along the apex and lateral facet of patella. Prominent trochlear and patellar osteophytes are demonstrated.

The medial patellar retinaculum is attenuated likely related to previous lateral dislocation and partial disruption. The lateral patellar retinaculum is intact.

There is a degenerative medial meniscal tear. There is maceration and linear signal seen in the posterior horn extending into the body. An oblique inferiorly surfacing tear of the body and posterior horn is a demonstrated. The finding is associated with severe chondral denuding and exuberant marginal osteophyte formation seen to the medial joint compartment. There is also subcortical edema seen to the weightbearing surface of the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau.

The lateral meniscus is macerated and not identified at the body and posterior horn. Findings are in keeping with extensive maceration and degenerative tearing of the body and the posterior horn of lateral meniscus. The finding is associated with denuding of the entire articular cartilage of lateral joint compartment associated with prominent lateral joint compartment osteophyte formation. There is also subcortical sclerosis and mild edema seen within the lateral joint compartment. An intraosseous cyst is seen to the lateral femoral condyle with 3 cm in keeping with subcortical tear.

The anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate and medial collateral ligament are intact.

The lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon appear intact.

There is a large knee effusion with reactive synovitis. There is no significant Baker's cyst. In the lateral popliteal fossa there is a large intraosseous loose body projecting anterior to the proximal fibers of the lateral head of the gastrocnemius measuring about 2.4 cm in maximum dimension. Smaller loose bodies are likely present in this region.

INTERPRETATION: 

Severe tricompartmental osteoarthritic change most severely affecting patellofemoral and lateral compartments. Degenerative meniscal tears laterally and medially with cartilaginous denuding to the lateral medial and patellofemoral compartments.

Loose bodies.

Patella alta with attenuation of the medial patellar retinaculum likely related to prior transient lateral dislocation of the patella.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain in right knee, primary osteoarthritis.
Comparison: [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.  

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Subchondral insufficiency fracture central weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle as well as the adjacent tibia with moderate bone marrow edema. No articular surface collapse or osteonecrosis. 
Subcortical cyst identified in the head of the fibula. Mild to moderate osteophyte formation within all 3 compartments of the knee.
Background bone marrow signal is normal. No aggressive osseous lesions.  

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate, partially ruptured Baker cyst. Moderate joint effusion. Diffuse synovial proliferation. No intra-articular bodies. 

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Large, complex tear of the body and posterior horn. There is marked extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Severe, diffuse cartilage loss. 

LATERAL COMPARTMENT: 
Lateral meniscus: Small tear at posterior root.  
Lateral compartment cartilage: Mild cartilage thinning and fissuring at the weightbearing aspect. 

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patella cartilage: Moderate to severe cartilage loss, lateral greater than medial.
Femoral trochlea cartilage: Mild to moderate cartilage thinning diffusely. 

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.  
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.  

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal. 
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal. 
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal. 

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Moderate tendinosis without tear.
Patella tendon: Mild tendinosis without tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: There is a mild amount of edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation.  No patella alta.  Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 11 mm. 

MUSCLES/TENDONS
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. 

SOFT TISSUES:
Varicose veins identified in the medial subcutaneous fat. 
Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

Compared to the prior exam, medial meniscal tear and chondrosis in the medial tibiofemoral compartment have progressed. Subchondral insufficiency fractures at the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau are new.

IMPRESSION: 

1. Subchondral insufficiency fractures at the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau.
2. Large, complex tear of the medial meniscus with marked extrusion. Small tear at the posterior root attachment of the lateral meniscus.
3. Tricompartmental chondrosis, most prominent in the medial tibiofemoral compartment.
4. Quadriceps and patellar tendinosis.
5. Moderate, ruptured Baker cyst.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE]  [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain for 7 months. No known injury.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. Acute subchondral insufficiency fracture at the weightbearing medial femoral condyle. Confluent subchondral bone marrow edema at the medial femoral condyle. Mild/early subchondral insufficiency fracture at the anteromedial tibial plateau. Normal background marrow signal. Proximal patellar enthesophytes.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion with synovitis. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Diffuse complex degenerative tearing of the medial meniscus. Superiorly displaced meniscal flap at the medial joint line and at the posterior horn. Severe meniscal extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Large confluent regions of full-thickness articular cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint. High-grade cartilage loss at the posterior medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Small complex tear of the lateral meniscal body, characterized by a dominant horizontal component.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage irregularity at the weightbearing aspect of the joint without focal defect.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Focal full-thickness chondral defect at the lateral patellar facet measuring 6 x 6 mm. Focal full-thickness fissuring at the patellar median ridge. Areas of full-thickness fissuring at the medial trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Periligamentous edema, likely related to adjacent pathology.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Chronic partial tearing at the femoral attachment of the fibular collateral ligament.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 15 mm, borderline elevated.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Intramuscular edema at the popliteus and tibialis anterior, possibly reflecting low-grade strains. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. Deep soft tissue edema at the posterior thigh. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Subchondral insufficiency fracture of the weightbearing medial femoral condyle without articular surface collapse. Mild/early subchondral insufficiency fracture at the anteromedial tibial plateau. 
2.	Moderate knee joint effusion with synovitis.
3.	Complex degenerative tearing throughout the medial meniscus with multiple displaced meniscal flaps and severe meniscal extrusion.
4.	Complex tearing of the lateral meniscal body.
5.	Tricompartmental chondrosis, severe in the medial compartment.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain for 2 to 3 months. No known injury.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Normal background marrow signal. No focal osseous lesion. Tricompartmental marginal osteophytosis.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. Moderate leaking multilobulated Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex tear with dominant radial component at the posterior root. Severe meniscal extrusion. No displaced meniscal flap or fragment.
Medial compartment cartilage: Confluent regions of high-grade articular cartilage loss at both sides of the weightbearing aspect of the joint, including some areas of full-thickness fissuring and associated subchondral signal changes. High-grade cartilage loss at the posterior medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: No tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage irregularity and high-grade cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint with regions of full-thickness fissuring and associated subchondral signal changes.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Diffuse articular cartilage loss at the patella, including areas of full-thickness cartilage loss at the median ridge, medial patellar facet, and lateral patellar facet. Full-thickness chondral fissuring at the medial and lateral trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear. Small intrasubstance ganglion formation at the tibial insertion.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 11 mm, normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Complex tear of the medial meniscus with dominant radial component at the posterior root. Severe meniscal extrusion.
2.	Tricompartmental osteoarthritis, worst at the medial tibiofemoral component, where it is severe. Small knee joint effusion. Moderate leaking multilobulated Baker's cyst.
